open.speaker: tn_archivist
lines: tn_archivist
The machine's in a mood, so it's ten pence a print and no promises. Sit there. Not that chair, that was the Thursday woman's, and I've gone a bit funny about it.
tn_archivist
Miss Jolliffe. Reference, local studies, and the fiche, which is me on my knees with a bulb. You've come about June 1973. Everybody does. Nobody asks for May.
ruth
'Nobody asks for May.' She's just told us where to look, dear, and made it sound like a complaint.

passives.line: The fiche is already wound to the first of June 1973. She didn't wind it for you. It was there when you came in.
The card drawer says LEVELS. Under the label, older ink, a different hand: MARSH (OTHER). Somebody renamed a thing to make it sound like a place.

options.text: May, then, since nobody asks. We'll sit in the other chair.
We'll have June, May, and whatever the Thursday woman had. Prints of all of it.
A chair you've gone funny about. In a library. We're in the right town.

chair.speaker: tn_archivist
lines: tn_archivist
...Thank you. Most people sit in it to be contrary. May is the 26th to the 29th. The bank holiday.
tn_archivist
The paper didn't print till the Friday after. June's where the words are. May's where it happened.

quiet.speaker: tn_archivist
lines: tn_archivist
This is a library. You'll have what I find, when the machine finds it, and you'll have it quietly.
miriam
We just shouted a print order at a woman with a bulb in her hand. Sit down.

hub.speaker: tn_archivist
lines: tn_archivist
Sandown library, local studies, since Miss Woodford started the collection in 1952 with a biscuit tin. I've got the tin. I've got most of what's happened here since. Ask.
hub.prompt: Miss Jolliffe waits with a hand on the fiche crank.

options.text: It's already wound to June '73. You read it this morning. You read it every year this week.
The Thursday woman. The good coat. What did she print, and what did she pay with?

fail.line: She printed page five. She paid ten pence. This is a library, not a bank.

options.text: 1927. The Survey drew a hut on the marsh and took it off the next sheet. Which edition, and who complained?
Ten pence, and the machine was in a mood. It came out, though. Thank you.
That's all for now, Miss Jolliffe.

static.line: The fiche is still turning and her hand's not on the crank. It's winding itself back to May. Let it. See where it stops.

wound.speaker: tn_archivist
lines: tn_archivist
...Every year. The 29th. I read page five and then I read the Sunnyside notice under it, and then I wind it back so nobody knows, except the machine, and now you.
tn_archivist
Miss Woodford was my aunt. She sat with me on the 30th of May 1973 and said, Margaret, write down everything you hear this week.
tn_archivist
Because they'll stop saying it by August, she said. They did.
ruth
Her aunt started a file and her niece kept the appointment. Two women and a biscuit tin against a whole town, dear. I'd back them.

wound_fail.speaker: tn_archivist
lines: tn_archivist
The machine remembers where it was left. I don't. Mr Prior at the newsagent's keeps the paper itself, if you'd rather handle it than read it.
teddy
We came from the newsagent. He sent us here. The town's got two readers and they send you to each other.

coat.speaker: tn_archivist
lines: tn_archivist
Page five, the Sunnyside notice, and the 1927 Ordnance sheet, which nobody's asked for since my aunt. Three prints. Thirty pence.
tn_archivist
She paid with a ten pence piece, a ten pence piece, and a ten pence piece. All three dated 1973.
tn_archivist
I've kept them in the tin. I'm not a fool and I'm not brave.
vera
Three coins minted the year of it, from a purse in 1994. Either she keeps old change, or she came with what she had.

survey.speaker: tn_archivist
lines: tn_archivist
...The 1927 six-inch. Sheet ninety-six south-east. A building drawn in the reeds past the sarsen, unnamed, and gone on the 1932 revision with no demolition noted.
tn_archivist
The drainage board complained: 'no such building'. The surveyor's reply is in my aunt's file, in his own hand, one line.
tn_archivist
'I stood in it. It had dials.' They retired him in '29.
tn_archivist
I've never shown anyone the reply. My aunt said people would come for it one day and I'd know them. I suppose this is me knowing.
vera
The Survey does not draw what is not there. A man stood in it, and said so, and lost his living. Fay is not the first.

survey_fail.speaker: tn_archivist
lines: tn_archivist
That's a question for the Survey, and the Survey's in Southampton, and they'll tell you what they told my aunt, which is nothing in triplicate.
tn_archivist
Read the shelf. The whole shelf. Then ask me again, if there's an again.
miriam
She's not refused. She's set homework. Red mark, though. That drawer stays shut on us.

print.speaker: tn_archivist
lines: tn_archivist
It usually does, for people who say thank you. Mind, your print's come out with the Sunnyside notice on it as well, which it shouldn't have, the frame's wrong for that.
tn_archivist
I'll not charge you for the notice. I've stopped being surprised by what that machine puts on a page.
june
A fiche that prints what it wasn't framed on. I'd like to look inside that machine. I'd like someone else to look first.
